context:
Make the budget derive from the thing that is actually constrained. Introduce
_CONTAINER_NAME_MAX_LEN = 64 and a replica-suffix budget, and have
compose_project_name accept the platform's longest service name so the project
budget becomes min(63, 64 - max_service_len - suffix - 1). The existing
sha1-truncation branch already produces a deterministic name once the budget is
right. Populate services=(...) for all 16 specs so the length is known without
parsing YAML at call time, with a test asserting the tuples match the compose
files. Add the guard test that enumerates every checked-in config x platform and
asserts the full container id fits.
description:
tests/uat/docker_assets.py bounds _PROJECT_NAME_MAX_LEN = 63 and truncates the
PROJECT name to fit. But the constrained identifier is the derived CONTAINER id,
`<project>-<service>-<replica>`, which mocker caps at 64 characters. The project
budget therefore leaves no room for the service and replica suffix.

MEASURED 2026-08-05 by enumerating every docker platform against the checked-in
release-gate configs:
  release-gate-02-docker-nonoltp: 13 of 16 platforms overflow (66-76 chars)
  release-gate-03-docker-oltp:    11 of 16 platforms overflow (65-76 chars)
Worst case, 76 chars:
  benchbox-uat-gate-release-gate-02-docker-nonoltp-lakesail-lakesail-connect-1

This means the canonical release-gate stages 2 and 3 have NEVER been runnable on
macOS/mocker as committed. It was masked on 2026-08-04 with an ad-hoc short-name
config; that workaround must not become the fix.

Longest service name across the matrix is `lakesail-connect` (16). Only lakesail
and velox declare `services=(...)` in their specs, so lengths for the other 14
platforms are only discoverable by parsing the compose files.

anti_patterns.instead: budget for a multi-character replica suffix
anti_patterns.why: a scaled service reaches -10 and silently overflows again by one character

anti_patterns.dont: fix this by shortening the checked-in config names or the docker_project_prefix
anti_patterns.instead: derive the project budget from the container-id limit and prove it with an enumerating test
anti_patterns.why: that is the 2026-08-04 workaround; it leaves the real bound wrong and silently re-breaks the moment anyone adds a longer config name or platform

anti_patterns.dont: hardcode 45 or any other magic project length
anti_patterns.instead: compute from _CONTAINER_NAME_MAX_LEN minus the actual per-platform service length
anti_patterns.why: it encodes today's longest service name (lakesail-connect, 16) as a constant nobody will revisit when a longer service appears

anti_patterns.instead: populate spec.services once at module load and pass the length in
anti_patterns.why: it is called on hot teardown paths and must stay pure and cheap

preserves.behavior: Docker (non-mocker) behavior is unchanged in practice -- the new bound is tighter, never looser.
Project names stay deterministic: the same (config, platform, prefix) always yields the same name, so teardown of a prior sweep still matches.
The _compose_base_command safety regex rejecting unsafe project names is unchanged.
docker_project_prefix stays operator-configurable; the fix must work for any prefix, not just the shorter one.

prior_art.concept: DockerPlatformSpec.services already exists and is honoured by compose up/pull/build argv; populating it for all platforms is the intended mechanism, not a new field
compose_project_name already implements deterministic sanitisation plus sha1 truncation; only the budget derivation is wrong -- extend, do not rewrite
existing project-name tests establish the naming contract; the new budget guard belongs alongside them
